title: Study impact of small features on DAG-MCNP performance
body:
The hypothesis is that small features in a model have a small impact on ray tracing performance thanks to the OBB Tree.

This stand along project includes a number of numerical experiments to test/validate/disprove this hypothesis.

Experiment 1-A: Start with a cube, modeled in both native MCNP and DAG-MCNP.  Add a "notch" to that cube at the corner, such as removing a rectangular prism from an edge.  The edge length of the notch is  d.  Repeat this with more notches of the same edge length.

Experiment 1-B: Similar to (1-A) but keep the total size of the detail fixed and the edge length shrinks as more notches are added.

Experiment 2-A,2-B: Repeat the above starting with a sphere and rectangular notches.

Experiment 3-A,3-B: Repeat experiment 2-(A,B) with other shaped details.

Determine which metrics will be compared, including at least the ray-firing time per ray.  Some experiment design will be necessary to determine fair measures of these quantities.

title: Repository redesign
body:
While the primary task to convert our SVN repository to a Git repository, there are a number of related tasks.

We currently have a number of related repositories:

**DAG-MCNP**

This private CAE-hosted repository is the primary repository for development of DAG-MCNP.  It contains all of the MCNP source code as well as the modifications for DAG-MCNP5.  The current layout of this repository should be redesigned as part of a transition to Git.  It currently contains a "vendor" directory which in turn contains a directory for each of three versions of MCNP5, as delivered by RSICC.  Parallel to "vendor" is a directory for each of those same versions, but modified by UW to generate DAG-MCNP5.  Those folders, in some cases, also contain the test for DAG-MCNP5, which can be quite large.

**DAGMC**

This public Github-hosted repository is intended as the primary repository for distribution of public DAGMC code and patches.  It should become the new home of the majority of our code.

**fusion_n_tools**

This private CAE-hosted repository contains many pieces, including the DAGMC_build directory.  This directory is historical place for the patch and other files we distribute publicly for DAG-MCNP5.
## Redesign

A new repository design will result in the following repositories:

**MCNP**

This will be a private CAE-hosted Git repository. It will contain the MCNP source code only.  It will have one branch for each version of MCNP, and each branch will be populated initially with the as-delivered source code from LANL/RSICC.  From their, we will add our modifications and patches.  This repo will only contain modified MCNP source code and will not contain any of the glue/wrapper code.  This code will be in the public DAGMC repository.  These branches will be derived from the different directories currently in the SVN repo.

**DAGMC**

This will be a public Github-hosted repository.  It will contain a different directory for each physics code.  Each of those directories will include a patch file (if available/appropriate) derived from a diff of the private physics code repository.  Each directory will also include the necessary glue/wrapper code and other additional files that we are free to distribute publicly.  This repository will be the primary development repository for those files.

**DAG-MCNP Testing**

This will be a public Github-hosted repository.  It will contain all the files necessary for testing of DAG-MCNP, including input files, reference output files and those scripts necessary to run all the tests.
## Preserving History

The goal of this redesign will be to preserve the development history that is currently built into the private DAG-MCNP repository.

title: Meshtally tag names should convey particle type

One potential problem with this is when both neutron and photon transport are done with the same mesh (e.g. the R2S-ACT workflow).  It would be a good idea to include particle type in the tag name.  TALLY_TAG_TYPE_erglow-erghigh would be the most straight-forward to parse.  Single letter types should be fine (n and p).

Unifying materials and densities in group names.
body:
The MC codes that I have personal experience with break into two factions when assigning materials and densities, either by a named material which is referred to by the code or with a number system. Therefore I pass on an idea like group naming of the form

```
mat_(ss316|1)_den_(mass|1.0)
mat_(water_pipes|51)_den_(atom|1.0e-3)
```

Or more generally

```
mat_(<material name>|<material_number>)_den_(<type_of_density>|<density_val>)
```

This covers both methods (known methods) of assigning material data to cells. It also is adaptable since we could always add more '|' symbols to the material name should we need more, with the benefits of simple string searching.

This relies on dagmc_preproc tagging volumes with this tag rather than creating material and density tags. We push the extracting of data from the group names to the physics code wrappers.

See #71 for the first set of test cases, also performed was testing in a spherical geometry. A spherical geometry containing 3 nested spheres of radii 10,20 and 30 cm were placed inside a hollow box of inner dimensions 100 and thickness 5. In vacuum we scored the track length flux in volumes 1 , 2 and 3 which correspond to the spheres of radii 10,20 and 30 cm. It appears that mgdraw.f gives us access to most of the Fluka variables at every particle substep. If I recall, the current implementation of advanced scoring works by waiting until the end of a history and allocating the track length backwards along the ray direction.

If we can wait until the end of the history then we can use usreou.f, which is called after the history is complete. By including the common block '(TRACKR)' we have access to all the data in the common block. If we need to do this after each history substep then using mgdraw.f would ideal.

title: USRBDX Define naming convention for multiple volume scorers
body:
Some Fluka scores, such as USTRACK and USRCOLL require a single volume within which to accumulate the scoring information. There are other scores that do require multiple volumes to be defined, the most important is USRBDX, which allows directional scoring of flux and current when crossing between 2 volumes.

I suggest a naming scheme something like

```
 USRBDX_PROTON_<vol_from>
        |-  Volume 1
        |-  Volume 2
       +-  Volume 7
```

Where <vol_from> is the region where particle are crossing from, and the volumes assigned to the groups are the "crossing to" volumes.

Alternatively we could create 2 groups for this type of score, eg

```
 USRBDX_PROTON_FROM
        |-  Volume 1
        |-  Volume 2
       +-  Volume 7
```

and

```
 USRBDX_PROTON_TO
        |-  Volume 2
        |-  Volume 1
       +-  Volume 1
```

Thus naming the boundary crossing esimator from 1 to 2, 2 to 1 and 7 to 1. Decide which makes the most sense, and which is most robust.

title: Nrmlwr fix, fixed issues seen with USRBDX
body:
The original implementation was incorrect, the fixes here rectify the problems with nrmlwr and solve #100.

Now, this may need some git magic to put right, I believe I have committed my change in the correct place.

I don't believe next_surf was being properly updated and restored based on g1wr, now the logic is
- upon entry set next_surf -> prev_surf (set on exit of the g1wr)
- if prop_step takes us across the boundary, next_step set by ray_fire
- if it does not we reset next_surf to be prev surf (as it was on entry)
- finally update prev_surf = next_surf for use in next entry

Furthermore, in nrmlwr, Fluka treats senses in the opposite fashion to mcnp 
- If sense == 1 i.e. foward of the cell, then we need to reverse the direction of the normal, since this is what fluka expects.

Testing seen in #100 show the issue is rectified.

I must review after step 1, while I am on the gh-pages branch.  The problem with this is I don't have the source file to make changes to as I review, so the workflow is somewhat convoluted.  I must make note of changes and edit after I get back to the source branch.

title: Implementation of processing of DETECT keyword
body:
The DETECT keyword should be implemented as a group name in a similar way to the materials are defined. However, in the case of the DETECT keyword we can define 

   1) Detectors 
   2) Detectors with (anti/)coincidence 

This is quite a complex card to define and thus requires a (relatively) complex syntax to define, in the FLUKA definition you must define
   a) the detector region
   b) the detectors that are to be taken in coincidence with the first region
   c) those to be taken in anti-coincidence 

This necessitates two related group names, for example

```
  S_DETECT_C12  (ie coincidence)
       |- Volume 1
       + Volume 3
  S_DETECT_A12  (anti-coincidence)
       |- Volume 2
       + Volume 4
```

Should be interpreted to be, create a Detector in region 12, where volumes 1 and 3 will be taken to be in coincidence with volume 12 and anti-coincidence with volumes 2 and 4. Thus producing 

```
  *...+....1....+....2....+....3....+....4....+....5....+....6....+....7....+....
  DETECT      0.0    <user defined stuff                  >    12.0 DET_12
  DETECT      0.0        -2.0      -4.0      1.0        3.0                &
```

Please note that the below is also valid input, since we only have to specify one coincident region ( in the group name)

```
  S_DETECT_A12  (anti-coincidence)
       |- Volume 2
       + Volume 4
```

Please ask if this is not clear.

title: Implementation of the RESNUCLE keyword
body:
The RESNUCLEI keyword should be implemented in a similar manner to materials. This is simple implementation, the volumes in which we would like to score should be added to a group called RESNUCLEI, 

```
 S_RESNUCLEI
            |-  Vol 2
            |-  Vol 4
            +-  Vol 9
```

Should produce 

```
  CARDNAME <user > unit# <user stuff> Volume index | Physical Volume | Detector name>
  RESNUCLE  <user defined stuff> 2.0 V2 RES_2
  RESNUCLE  <user defined stuff> 4.0 V4 RES_4
  RESNUCLE  <user defined stuff> 9.0 V9 RES_9
```

NOTE: The actual volume of the region should be placed in V2/V4 etc

NOTE:: The unit number should be the first free unit number, I think we actually need a function that determines the first unused unit number, all these detectors should be placed in the same unit number.

title: Implementation of USRCOLL
body:
USRCOLL should be implemented in a similar method to material handling, this is a simple detector to process. Using the following group name convention

```
S_USRCOLL_<Particle name>
      |-  Volume 2
      |-  Volume 4
      +-  Volume 5
```

Should produce 

```
   USRCOLL  <blank> <blank> <first free unit number> <volume index> <volume> <blank> COL_index
   USRCOLL  <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> &
```

eg for volume 2

```
    USRCOLL  <blank> <blank>    -21.0         2.0   32.0e5  <blank> COL_2
    USRCOLL  <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> &
```

title: Implementation of USRTRACK
body:
USRTRACK should be implemented in a similar way to materials, see #88, in summary

```
 S_USRTRACK_<particle name>
                |- Volume 2
                +-  Volume 4
```

Should produce 

```
 USRTRACK <blank> <particle number> <free unit #> <region index> <volume> <blank> <name>
 USRTRACK <blank> <blank>  <blank> <blank>  <blank> <blank> &
```

title: Implementation of USRYIELD
body:
USRYIELD should be implemented in a similar way to material handling. USRYIELD is a complex 2d score of doubly differential particle yield.

```
S_USRYIELD_<particle type>_<Vol ID>
        +  Vol_IDS
```

In a similar way to USRBDX scoring, you must define a from and a to, I think the most simple way is have the <Vol ID> as the from, and the ones listed in the group as to's, eg.

```
S_USRYIELD_MUON_79
          +  Vol 81
```

Should produce

```
  USRYIELD <blank> MUON -21.0 81.0 79.0 <blank> YLD_79_81
```

NOTE: again uses the next free unit number to provide the output unit, the name should be defined as from and to.

title: Implementation of USRTRACK
body:
Processing of USRTRACK scorers should be handled in a similar way to other scorers, groupnames should be of the form

```
 S_USRTRACK_<PARTICLE>
              + Volume Ids
```

Thus when processed 

```
 USRTRACK <blank> <particle> <unit number> <region id> <volume> <blank> TRK_vol_id
 USRTRACK <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> &
```

For example, if the group names were

```
   S_USRTRACK_MUON
            + Volume 23
   S_USRTRACK_KAON
            + Volume 44
```

We should produce

```
USRTRACK <blank> MUON -21 23.0 <volume> <blank> TRK_23
USRTRACK <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> &
USRTRACK <blank> KAON -22 44.0 <volume> <blank> TRK_44
USRTRACK <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> <blank> &
```

title: Upgrade of DAGMC code to MOAB Trunk

Having recently re-installed all our software trunk and installing the bleeding edge versions, I've found that the trunk of MOAB makes many of our DAGMC calls non functional due to additional arguments to certain functions, e.g. 

```
 build_tree( all_tets, kdtree_root );

The current trunk calls this an error, needing an additional argument to be compatible with the current trunk version of MOAB. This presents a bit of an issue for us, now meaning we may need some macros and ifdefs and possibly versioning in branches.

title: SL6 Build And Test
body:
I am creating a separate issue for adding Scientific Linux 5 and 6 platforms to the BaTLab so as not to delay implementation of the continuous build system.

While the cmake version issue is easily resolved (see Issue #166), there seems to be a default compiler issue as well.  When I tried to build fludag on SL6 thousands of lines like the one below:

make
/slots/08/dir_64196/userdir/FLUKA/libflukahp.a(flukam.o): In function `flukam':
/home/alfredo/fluprogfor/mainmvax/flukam.f:1232: undefined reference to`_gfortran_transfer_character_write'

I didn't get these messages for SL5, but it also failed.  

A google search on the message brought me to FLUKA's mailing list, where the following response was posted:

```
From: Giuseppe Battistoni <Giuseppe.Battistoni_at_mi.infn.it> 
Date: Fri, 03 Feb 2012 08:55:05 +0100
Dear Mina 
Unfortunately, as previously reported in our discussion list in the last 2 o 3 months, 
we have the gfortran version of FLUKA only for gfortran versions 4.5 or 4.6 
(fluka2011.2-linux-gfor64bit-gcc451-AA and fluka2011.2-linux-gfor64bitAA respectively) 
We found that the us of gfortran compiler in version 4.4 (or earlier) gives rise to 
important bugs. 
For unknown reasons gfortran developers decided to change a lot of internal names 
in recent versions, and that is the reason of those error messages. 
Therefore, either you upgrade to gcc4.5 (or better gcc4.6) or you stick to the old good 
32-bit g77 version. 
        Giuseppe Battistoni 
```

The gcc compiler that SL6 downloads with it's built-in Software Update program is 4.4.7.3, so this is why the build is failing.

I have installed SL6 on my VirtualBox on my Mac laptop.  To test a compilation process using gcc 4.6.4 I downloaded the distribution, but ran out of space on my virtual hard drive.  On Scientific Linux under Virtual Box the default virtual disk size is 8 Gigabytes.  From StackOverflow it is possible to increase the size of the virtual disk for an installed virtual machine, but then one has to update the partition size using a piece of third party software called Gparted.  It looks a little dicey but I might try it.

The easier route, which I think is possible, but I'm not sure, is to create a new SL6 virtual machine and increase the size of the virtual disk prior to the install.  Then go through the process again.  I have enough room on my mac to make the virtual disk 45 Gb, which ought to be big enough.

title: Improve Energy Bin Search
body: The current energy bin search for DAGMC tallies (Tally::get_energy_bin) uses a linear approach.  Consider implementing a binary search instead to improve efficiency.

title: Extend data structure for TallyData
body:
DAGMC tallies currently store their data as three std::vector objects:
- tally_data: total sum of scores
- error_data: total sum of squares of scores
- temp_tally_data: sum of scores for one history

The size of each of these vectors is the number of tally points multiplied by the number of energy bins.  This limits the maximum size of the tallies that can be defined.  It may be worth looking into an alternative, more multidimensional data structure.  This data structure could also allow for future expansion - such as adding time or angle binning, or allowing for more than one tally multiplier per tally.

title: Improve access to TallyData for MPI
body:
Currently, the TallyData of a DAGMC tally is accessed through methods in TallyManager.  These tallies are stored in a map that is searched every time by index to get the current status of the data that is needed for MPI methods in DAG-MCNP5.

It may be worth considering adding some sort of iterator to the TallyManager rather than needing to do this search when a lot of tallies have been added as observers.  Alternatively, the unordered map from C++11 could be more efficient than the standard map as it is implemented using a hash table instead of a binary tree.

title: Tally tag format
body:
It looks like the current output format for DAGMC tally tags is "TALLY_TAG_" followed by the floating point energy bounds deliminted by a "-".

I think this format is non-ideal for several reasons:
1. Sorting order is not guaranteed. Consider this portion of `mbsize -t` output:

```
TALLY_TAG_0.907-0.962   150110
TALLY_TAG_0.962-1   150110
TALLY_TAG_1-1.11   150110
TALLY_TAG_1.07e-05-1.37e-05   150110
```
1. Tag names cannot be easily parsed with a "-" delimiter because "-" is also used in exponents (`TALLY_TAG_2.26e-05-2.9e-05`).
2. Tag names cannot be parsed by fixed width either.

I think results should be tagged to mesh with a single vector tag. The energy bounds could be tagged as a rootSet tag. I understand this makes visualization less convenient, but it seems it would be much easier to explode vector tags out into the current form then the other way around (for the aforementioned reasons).

title: First demonstration of UW workflow with Tech-X interface
body:
A collaboration with Tech-X, funded by NASA/Wyle, to provide a graphical front end for manipulation and preparation of DAGMC geometry under the UW Unified Workflow (UW)<sup>2</sup>

Depends on other issues identified in https://github.com/svalinn/DAGMC/milestones/Initial%20Tech-X%20integration
# Workflow assumptions

The high level user interaction can be described as:
1. User begins with an faceted (h5m) representation of the geometry that has been imprinted, merged and includes a "graveyard" volume
2. User will use graphical interface to:
      a. assign materials to volumes
      b. define tally objects and assign volumes or surfaces to those objects
3. User will save a version of the faceted geometry file with additional metadata defined in 2.
4. User will run physics package P using this annotated geometry file
## Material assignment

Material assignment is governed by the following:
1. A library of available materials will be provided to populate a list of materials available to the user, based on human readable material names
2. Each non-vacuum volume will be assigned a material using the PyNE material assignment conventions adopted by DAGMC:
      a. tagging the meshset for the volume with a string containing the material name
      b. creating a new meshset for each unique material that is used in a problem and adding the volume meshset for each volume that contains said material to that material's meshet
3. The user may assign a material density to any volume, thus overriding the default material density as defined in the material library.
## Tally Object Creation

Only "raw" tallies will be supported at this time: e.g. tallies based on the particle tracks directly without multiplying by physical quantities.  To be clear, current/fluence/flux will be supported and dose/energy deposition/etc will not be supported at this time.
1. Each region of interest (volume or surface) will be assigned a tally object identified by the type of particle being scored in that object
## Source definition

Particle source characteristics will be defined using a finite set of parameters that users can define using a graphical interface.  Those parameters can be attached to the geometry file (h5m) using some tagging convention.

MCNP5 kcode meshtally bug
body:
It seems that performing a continue run of a kcode calculation with a tetmesh tally is different than for a fixed source problem. In fixed source if the simulation did not complete, but there are tally dumps in the runtpe file, then one can do the following

```
continue
nps -1
```

This will dump the tally data as if the simulation were finished. However in kcode, instead of this, the code loads the contents of each dump into a new meshtally instance, and then once all rendezvous are loaded, the contents are presumably written to file. This for one, is unexpected behaviour, two in the test example the simulation ran out of memory.

body: Originally the UWUW class determined if there were materials and tallies by trying to read them using the full from_hdf5 methods, these methods raise an exception if they fail, thus the function was wrapped in a try/except block. title: DATAPATH and xsdir command line argument not working as intended
body:
My understanding is that there are two ways to specify where your data is for a run:
- 1. Set the $DATAPATH environment variable, and MCNP will search for a file called "xsdir" in that path.

When doing this, MCNP always finds xsdir, but it doesn't always find the cross section library specified in xsdir. Specifically, if $DATAPATH is the same as it was during compilation, it will find the cross sections, but if it is different, then it will not.
- 2. Specify "xsdir=" on the command line, and MCNP will use the specified file.

This appears to work only if the file specified is in the same directory as the one where MCNP is run. So if the files "testdir1" and "testlib1" are in the current directory, then using "xsdir=testdir1" will work. But if testdir1 and testlib1 are 2 levels down, using "xsdir=../../testdir1" will not work.

The reason any of this matters is that some of the tests in DAG-MCNP-TESTING have command line arguments like "xsdir=../../testdir1", and MCNP isn't finding the cross sections.

title: Complete the PyNE Tally Class
body:
The Tally class was originally implemented to allow an arbitrary particle from the pyne::particle class to be used in a pyne::tally object, it was envisioned originally that this would end up with allowing us to use Cubit/Trelis groups in the following style

tally:Neutron/DPA
tally:Photon/Heat
tally:Proton/Dose
tally:Neutron/HeProd
etc

These particle type/tally type pairs would have to figure out a number of things, for example
- DPA - needs to know the average displacement energy & the material of the cell where DPA is calculated
- Dose 
- EffectiveDose - needs to know the dose response function
- Heat - needs to know the material of the cell

What I imagine for the case of DPA, we can use material object metadata to store the displacement energy on material by material basis, i.e this must already set in the material object at runtime, perhaps we can assume the average for most materials (40 eV) as a default but warn that otherwise it isn't set.

For tally types that require the material number, by the time we write the lcad file, we know what the material number for each cell is, and therefore we can determine the appropriate material number for say an FM card in the case of MCNP

Fluka Importance splitting applies to 4 categories of particles 
- All particles
- hadrons, heavy ions and muons
- electrons, positrons and photons
- low energy neutrons

Following a unified approach with UWUW, the user will be able to add volumes to a group in the form, 
Importance:Neutron/1.0, or Importance:Muon/0.25 for example. The Fluka part will have to figure out if what category that particle falls into and then produce the appropriate BIASING card.

title: Reintroduce simple workflow
Improve DagGeant4 performance
body:
DagGeant4 performance needs to be increased. A full suite of profiling should be done for a typical DAGMC problem, but I think the problem is related to the lack of a hierarchy to the DagSolids. Typical Geant4 geometry is hierarchical, i.e. a mother volume has a number of children, so when a ray fire is done it is done only against the volumes at the same level as the mother, once inside the mother it only fires at the child volumes, etc. However with DagGeant4 as we have no other information to go one, we assume everything is on the same level as the mother volume, which of course in our case it is since we have a flat geometry due to "imprint and merge".

There are two solutions to the problem, either:
- We introduce the concept of a hierarchy, perhaps using something like moab::GenerateHierarchy to figure out which volumes lie inside of others
- Or use the imprint and merge information as part of the Geant4 transport process

My preference is the second, this is the route recommended by the John Apostolakis, this requires modification to geant4::Navigator, implimenting our own geant4::dag navigator. This is needed as each  whilst each DagSolid object has a concept of which volumes bound it because of the rich collection of information in Dagmc, the traditional navigator has no way of using this information, and thus every rayfire call starts at the mother volume, it must then fire at every dagsolid in the problem and then choose the smallest distance.

title: Legacy MCNP ACIS importance tagging doesn't work for certain MCNP6 particles
body:
ACIS volumes are added to groups like `imp.n_1` to specify that the neutron importance for that volume is 1. MCNP5 only `n`, `p`, and `e` particle types, so this works fine. MCNP6, however, has quite a few more particle types, some of which are symbols. Two of these symbols, `|` and `~`, cause problems. This is what happens when you try to assign a group with the name of `imp.|_1` to a volume:

```
CUBIT> group "imp.|_1" add volume 1
WARNING: Entity name 'imp.|_1' can't be used in commands.
         Additional name 'imp.__1' assigned.
Creating imp.__1 (Group 2)
Group Entity 'imp.__1', 'imp.|_1' (Id = 2)
It owns/encloses 1 entity: 1 volume.
Journaled Command: group "imp.|_1" add volume 1
```

The group actually assigned ends up being `imp.__1` instead.

However, it turns out that if we switched the naming scheme to replace the `.` with a `:` and the `_` with a `=`, all of the MCNP6 particle types will work:

```
CUBIT> group "imp:|=1" add volume 1
WARNING: Entity name 'imp:|=1' can't be used in commands.
         Additional name 'imp___1' assigned.
Creating imp:|=1 (Group 2)
Group Entity 'imp:|=1', 'imp___1' (Id = 2)
It owns/encloses 1 entity: 1 volume.
Journaled Command: group "imp:|=1" add volume 1
```

The warning message still shows up, but the correct group name is assigned.

Thus I propose to change the naming scheme from `imp.n_1` to `imp:n=1`. This also has the advantage of being the exact same way you would specify importances on an MCNP cell card.

Some background: Regression tests for `make_watertight` are in a separate [repository](https://github.com/pshriwise/mw_reg) because they rely on models which we can't make publicly accessible. Currently, the models are kept in CAE space and are required to be gathered by the user if they want to run the regression tests. These tests are run weekly on my work machine with an indicator to me if they fail. (This is a separate problem to be faced later.)

Problem at hand: The regression test repository builds a test program for the models based on a lot of the `make_watertight` code. As such, it would be nice to have the same capability with the version of `make_watertight` here in DAGMC. There are multiple ways to do this, but before I embark on any of them I'd like to figure out which is best:

1) In make_watertight's previous home, [moab_tools](https://github.com/svalinn/moab_tools) I wrote a branch which created a library of the critical functions for `make_watertight` and built my test program using that. I could repeat this in DAGMC. This might require the installation of some make_watertight headers which could be done under their own `make_watertight` directory.

2) I could bring the test program into DAGMC and build it here to run my test scripts for the regression test models using that program instead. 

If there are other suggestions for better methods of going about this please feel free to suggest them here!

title: [make_watertight] fix trelis sphere unit test
body:
This PR contains a few changes to make_watertight and a new unit test for make_watertight to address issues #436 and #437

Summary of changes:
- upon deleting a surface, make_watertight now looks at all parent volumes of the surface to check if this was the last surface used to define that volume. If so, the volume is deleted along with the surface. (This condition is reached when there are no curves for the surface, so the curve sets should already be taken care of.)
- make_watertight now accepts the existence of a volume without curves so long as the following conditions are met:
  1) one of its parent volumes is composed of a single surface which is the surface w/o curves
  2) the surface of that volume contains a watertight set of triangles (this is verified by confirming that there are no skin edges returned by the find_skin operation in make_watertight)
- an addition of a unit test for make_watertight which is a sphere produced in Trelis containing no geometric curves. The test verifies that make_watertight reports a successful sealing of the model and that the volume is not deleted in the process.

title: [make_watertight] Refactor namespaces to classes and add library.
body:
This PR:

1) Alters the structure of `make_watertight` s.t. the `gen`, `arc`, `zip`, `cleanup`, `cw_func`, and `mw_func` namespaces are all now classes. The aim is to allow `make_watertight` to be applied on top of other applications by passing a MOAB interface pointer to the class rather than having it create its own or passing the interface pointer down to each function.

2) Adds a library for `make_watertight` functionality and installs all headers associated with that functionality. Right now these headers are installed in the dagmc `include` directory, but I could also see them going in a sub-directory in the includes dir named something like "make_watertight" or "mw" and am open to that change.

3) This also removes some old test programs/files that are non-essential.

Some of the lower classes like `Gen`, `Zip`, etc. are highly dependent on each other and as such it was difficult to immediately imagine a clear hierarchy for inheritance of classes up to the `MakeWatertight` and `CheckWatertight` level. The result is that some classes will contain instances of each other to account for this. Design change suggestions to help with this problem are very welcome!

title: Check for OBB tag in have_obb_tree
body:
Currently there are two tags to identify the existence of an OBB Tree. One is the OBB tag which stores box data on an entity set representing a node in the tree. The other is OBB_TREE which is used to associate a tree root with a volume entity handle. 

DAGMC only checks for the existence of the OBB_TREE tag. While this is what functionally connects DAGMC to the OBB Trees, if the OBB tag does not exist then there is no box data to look up when traversing the tree and the process will fail rapidly. Both tags should be searched for in this method.

If the OBB tag is not found, then the OBB_TREE tag should be removed (deleted) because at this point the root sets are meaningless without actual box data and the OBB Tree will be initialized as usual.

title: Enforce more strict code formatting
body:
The new version of astyle (3.0) has a few default options files which format code to specific style guides. One of them is google style, which attempts to follow the [google style guide](https://google.github.io/styleguide/cppguide.html) as closely as possible. The options it uses are in [`tools/astyle/file/google.ini`](https://github.com/ljacobson64/DAGMC/blob/strict_formatting/tools/astyle/file/google.ini). Note that this is different from simply using `--style=google`, which only deals with brace formatting.

I have set it up so that the CI will run astyle using the options in `google.ini`. The CI will also run the style guide check before running the rest of the tests, so that we don't have to wait as long to find out about a style guide failure.

title: Cleanup cmake
body:
I guess there's no better time to submit this than during a hackathon...

* Default to a Release build. This results in optimization flags being used everywhere as appropriate. MCNP is still configured to use no more than `-O1`.
* Rearrange directory structure. Anything with source code is now in its own subdirectory under the `src/` directory.
* Add macros to `cmake/DAGMC_macros.cmake`. This results in much less duplicated cmake elsewhere. For example, the `dagmc_install_library` macro contains all the functionality needed to install a static and shared library at the same time without requiring lots of extra code to be added for every library we build.
* Change how we find HDF5 and MOAB libraries. Previously they were required to be in users' `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, but the intended use for `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` is for executables to locate libraries at runtime, not compile time. Now, users can specify a `-DHDF5_ROOT` and `-DMOAB_ROOT` when running cmake. The old `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` functionality still works but is deprecated.
* Stop using the CMake file provided by MOAB because it always seems to cause problems for people. Now the DAGMC cmake simply looks for files called `libmoab.so` and `libmoab.a` in the directory specified by `-DMOAB_ROOT`.
* Add `RPATH` functionality so that all executables and libraries automatically know where their dependencies, including compilers, are located. This removes the need for users to add anything to their `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. This is currently not working for anything that links to Geant4 libraries, and I don't know why.
* Add options to disable building optional targets such as astyle and make_watertight. The default is still to build them as before.
* Remove the mcnpfuncs internal library and replace it with an object library. I think this is a more appropriate way to handle it.
* Remove old, unused, and/or broken things.

Everything listed here works on Linux, but I can't vouch for Mac. Although, from what I have heard, the Mac build is currently broken anyways so this doesn't really change anything in that regard.

title: New cmake
body:
New version of #535.

* Default to a Release build. This results in optimization flags being used everywhere as appropriate. MCNP is still configured to use no more than `-O1`.
* Add macros to `cmake/DAGMC_macros.cmake`. This results in much less duplicated cmake elsewhere. For example, the `dagmc_install_library` macro contains all the functionality needed to install a static and shared library at the same time without requiring lots of extra code to be added for every library we build.
* Change how we find HDF5 and MOAB libraries. Previously, HDF5 was required to be in users' `$PATH` and MOAB was required to be in users' `$LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. Now, users must specify `-DMOAB_DIR` when running cmake, and cmake automatically finds the location of the HDF5 that was used when building MOAB. The `$PATH` and `$LD_LIBRARY_PATH` do not need to be edited.
* Add `RPATH` functionality so that all executables and libraries automatically know where their dependencies are located. This removes the need for users to add anything to their `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`. This functionality can be turned off.
* Add options to disable building optional targets such as astyle and make_watertight. The default is still to build them as before.
* Remove the mcnpfuncs internal library and replace it with an object library. I think this is a more appropriate way to handle it.
* Update documentation to reflect changes

title: Remove mangling
body:
This PR removes the need for name mangling in `meshtal_funcs.h` by making use of `bind(c)` in `fmesh_mod.F90`. Previously, there was a macro in `meshtal_funcs.h` that attempted to determine the correct name mangling, but I've found situations where it didn't work properly. This is a much simpler way to do it.

(spoilers)

The real reason I did this is that MCNP6.2 uses Fortran2003, and from what I can tell, Intel's name mangling scheme for Fortran2003 is slightly different than it is for Fortran90. (It could be caused by something else, but regardless, the mangling is different between MCNP6.2 and all other versions of MCNP.) Trying to fix the name mangling macro would be pretty ugly because a different name mangling would need to be used for DAG-MCNP5 (Fortran90) than DAG-MCNP6.2 (Fortran2003) when trying to build both at the same time. This PR completely removes that problem, and it will remove any future problems related to name mangling as well.

I've gotten DAG-MCNP6.2 working (or at least compiling) on top of these changes, but support for that will come in a future PR.

title: DAGMCNP6 compiler bug
body:
Hi all

I am trying to compile DAGMCNP with mcnp version 6.1.1 beta and came across a few errors

```
[ 97%] Building Fortran object src/mcnp/mcnp6/CMakeFiles/mcnp6.dir/Source/src/partisn/partisn_read_xslibb.F90.o
[ 97%] Building C object src/mcnp/mcnp6/CMakeFiles/mcnp6.dir/Source/src/utils/c_ioroutines.c.o
[ 97%] Linking Fortran executable mcnp6
/usr/bin/x86_64-linux-gnu-ld: cannot find -lieee
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
src/mcnp/mcnp6/CMakeFiles/mcnp6.dir/build.make:25110: recipe for target 'src/mcnp/mcnp6/mcnp6' failed
make[2]: *** [src/mcnp/mcnp6/mcnp6] Error 1
CMakeFiles/Makefile2:1506: recipe for target 'src/mcnp/mcnp6/CMakeFiles/mcnp6.dir/all' failed
make[1]: *** [src/mcnp/mcnp6/CMakeFiles/mcnp6.dir/all] Error 2
Makefile:129: recipe for target 'all' failed
make: *** [all] Error 2
jshim@jshim-B250M-D3H:~/dagmc_bld/DAGMC/DAGMC/bld$ 
```
It appears that gfortran-7 / gcc-7 no longer accepts the -mieee-fp flag

I have commented out the following line in the mcnp/mcnp6/CMakeLists.txt file and this works for my particular system
```
set(CMAKE_Fortran_FLAGS "${CMAKE_Fortran_FLAGS} -mieee-fp")  
```

However others have had the same issue and solved it like this [https://sourceforge.net/p/plplot/mailman/message/36155710/](https://sourceforge.net/p/plplot/mailman/message/36155710/) - it appears that glibc has dropped that particular part of addressing IEEE rounding and is now native to the glibc library. Since this is sensitive to the glibc version, this implies a linux distro/version issue. However the fix in the above link should fix that problem, I think?

I have discussed this with @makeclean

title: Cannot build static executables with system HDF5
body:
It is not possible to build static executables using MOAB built with system HDF5. The error messages that occur look like this:

```
/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libsz.a(sz_compat.o): In function `SZ_BufftoBuffCompress':
(.text+0x149): undefined reference to `aec_buffer_encode'
(.text+0x339): undefined reference to `aec_buffer_encode'
```

The issue is that system HDF5 links to another library called `sz`, while custom HDF5 builds do not (at least by default). CMake's `FindHDF5` macro correctly identifies whether `sz` needs to be added to the `HDF5_LIBRARIES` variable, but it does not pick up on the fact that `sz` itself is linked to another library: `aec`. This is the problem.

The reason CI doesn't fail because of this is that we don't use system HDF5 on CI. We build our own HDF5.

I tested what happens if you build your own HDF5 but enable `sz`, and then build MOAB on that HDF5, and then build DAGMC on that MOAB. The same issue appears: it doesn't know that it needs to look for `aec`.

I don't know the best way to fix this. We could manually add `aec` to our `HDF5_LIBRARIES` variable, but this doesn't seem like a good idea though since not all systems will need it. Perhaps we could check what's in `HDF5_LIBRARIES`, and if it finds `sz`, manually add `aec` too?

* A Dockerfile has been added for Ubuntu 18.04.

    * Ubuntu 16.04 vs. 18.04
    * gcc vs. clang
        * gcc-5.3 on 16.04; gcc-7.3 on 18.04
        * clang-3.8 on 16.04; clang-6.0 on 18.04
    * MOAB 5.1.0 vs. master

title: DAGMC Geometry Statistics
body:
**GOAL:** 

Provide a script that will analyze a DAGMC geometry and report a summary of its features and complexity.

**Background**

DAGMC geometries are composed, fundamentally, of triangular facets that collectively represent geometric surfaces, where those surfaces are combined to represent geometric volumes.  A collection of volumes represents a real engineering model upon which radiation transport analysis is performed.  The computational performance of the DAGMC algorithm depends on some set of features of these tessellated geometric models, but the particular set of features has not been widely studied.  

In addition, users and potential users are often interested in understanding the range of complexity of DAGMC models that have been demonstrated/used in practice.  While it is sometimes possible to share graphical representations of those models, they are occasionally considered proprietary information.  In the absence of a visual representation, the complexity and scale of a model can be described by a set of features of that model.

This project will create a tool that will read a model and calculate features of that model in a standard way for reporting among the community of DAGMC users and developers.

**Approach**

This tool will be a Python script, relying on pymoab for access to details of any given model.  In some cases, the tool will simply count entities and report their number.  In other cases, the tool will perform calculations on those entities to derive additional metrics.

Possible metrics include, but are not limited to:

- number of triangles, surfaces, volumes
- distribution of aspect ratio of triangles, surfaces, volumes
- distribution of scale length of triangles, surfaces, volumes
- distribution of number of triangles/surface and surfaces/volume (including implicit complement)
- distribution of valence in nodes of model

An initial version of the tool can be generated with a small set of metrics, and expanded over time.  Most initial metrics will be matters of implementation, but there may be research questions about which metrics best describe a model, both in general and in the context of the DAGMC algorithms.

title: Detect enclosed volumes
body:
Feature/Problem: This feature request is related to the possible problem of completely enclosed volumes.  It may be possible for an imported geometry to include two volumes that overlap because one volume is completely enclosed within another.  This would represent an upstream flaw in the model creation, but it would be valuable if such a flaw were detected before running the problem.  A model with such features will run successfully with no indications of an error, but the results are not reliable.  This is a special case of overlapping geometries, and perhaps a new feature should be prepared to detect all overlapping geometries.

Solutions: Capability can be created either within an existing tool or in a new tool that will test for this kind of overlap (or all kinds of overlaps).  

The brute force solution is to test every vertex of every surface to ensure that it is not included in any volume.  In a watertight geometry, such a test would exclude the volumes that are known to contain the vertex on its boundary.  Such a test is probably prohibitively expensive.

There may be capability within Cubit/Trelis that can be invoked to detect overlaps, and user documentation should be updated to advise such a test in the workflow.

title: Assignment of material's temperature by python code should be remained when using DAGMC-OpenMC
body:
Hi All,
    New feature of using CAD-Based Geometries have been released in latest version. However, the way of assigning temperature have changed. We can not assign material's temperature by:

```
u235 = openmc.Material(name="fuel")
u235.add_nuclide('U235', 1.0, 'ao')
u235.set_density('g/cc', 11)
u235.temperature = 900         #This line will be no use even if you add it
```

   Materials' temperature can not be assigned, the only way to assign temperature is by using "Cubit/Trelis" when we creating geometry model:

`CUBIT> group "temp:900" add vol x` ([here is the link](https://svalinn.github.io/DAGMC/usersguide/codes/openmc.html#temperatures))

Thus, it will be very inconvenient when we want to change the materials' temperature, we have to launch "Cubit/Trelis" to modify it. In particular, if we want to achieve a coupling between the neutronics and thermal-hydraulics(such as between OpenMC and a thermal-hydraulics code), we need exchange the power distribution, materials' temperature and density distribution by editing script. It is impossible to exchange large amounts of data manually by launching "Cubit/Trelis" and enter "`CUBIT> group "temp:900" add vol x`" every time. So I highly recommend that assignment of material's temperature by python code should be remained when using DAGMC-OpenMC.

Best Regards,
Benjamin

title: Overlap Check Tool
body:
Someone at the DagMC workshop in Madison mentioned an overlap check tool for discretized DAGMC models. I'm in the process of polishing up a version of this now - just need to add tests. I'm creating this issue to avoid work duplication and make everyone aware of the method I intend to use. 

First, the tool will check all vertices of the problem for containment by more than one volume. My plan is that this will be the default mode. Optionally, users can provide a certain number of points to check along each triangle edge as well. While more thorough, this takes quite a bit of extra time - hence it being an optional approach. Output from the program will make users aware of this option if it is not enabled, as checking the edges of the triangles will make the search more robust.

My thinking on triangle edges is that as the number of points we check on the edges approaches infinity, we should find all overlap (to within machine precision) - i.e. points in the middle of the triangle shouldn't matter because the extent and orientation of the triangle is defined by its edges. I could definitely be missing something there though, so please let me know if there's something more I should look into.

title: Overlap Check Tool
body:
## Description
This PR implements the overlap checking tool discussed in #639.

I've tested it on FNG, ATR, & UWNR (several models we know are successfully imprinted, merged, and sealed) to ensure that overlaps are *not* found for those cases. I've also included a few test cases here to make sure it will find overlaps successfully - more details below.

### Building

Unlike other executables in the repo, I've opted not to build a library for the overlap tool. I didn't see a compelling case for someone using this as a library, but I could be swayed otherwise.

### Test cases

I've added a few tests here to make sure that we find overlaps when we should.

  - A sphere overlapping a box
  - A cylinder and cube with coincident surfaces, unimprinted
  - A cylinder and cube with coincident surfaces, imprinted
  - One cylinder completely enclosing another
  - A slight overlap (1E-06 thickness) between a cylinder and box*

* - This overlap was too small to be detected using Trelis' default settings, but is caught by the overlap tool. Were imprinting to be used, no overlap would exist, but this was more to represent a case where imprinting might fail due to topological problems in the CAD model.

There are probably more test cases that would be useful here too, but I don't have the bandwidth to look into that right now.

### Bumping locations

I'm sure this will come up in the review, so I'll address it early. There are cases in which MOAB really doesn't like it if rays are fired through vertices. A lot of nasty output occurs which we cannot turn off. Rather than force users to suffer through this output, I bump the test location a bit and make sure we are firing rays away from the vertex's surface to avoid that output. I understand that this isn't ideal, but I think it's the best thing to do until that problem is resolved in MOAB.

Example of this output:

```
Vertex 667:
Global id = 0

title: `DAGMC_LIBRARIES` CMake variable incorrectly populated
body:
**Describe the Bug**
Currently, all libraries are added to the `DAGMC_LIBRARIES` CMake variable whether they are enabled or not. This is caused by [these lines](https://github.com/svalinn/DAGMC/blob/8b23e5fd12dfa59e490a661a054b92722db56f18/cmake/DAGMC_macros.cmake#L225). As these macros get evaluated and inserted into the various directories where it is called, the `DAGMC_LIBRARIES` variable is populated regardless of whether or not the library is enabled or disabled. [`add_subdirectory`](https://cmake.org/cmake/help/v3.0/command/add_subdirectory.html) will keep targets from being added to the project, but the subdirectory `CMakeLists.txt` file will still be processed. **To Reproduce**
Clone the repo and run `cmake -DBUILD_TALLY=OFF`. You will still see `dagtally` in the list of DAGMC libraries in the `DAGMCConfig.cmake` file in the directory where you've run this command. **Expected Behavior**
Only enabled libraries are added to the `DAGMC_LIBRARIES` variable.

    - [ ] OpenMC
    - [ ] Geant4

A written model preparation tutorial is being prepared by @NybergWISC, so creating some of these tutorials would be a good extension of that work.

title: Automatic graveyard generation
body:
Graveyards can be problematic when working with DAGMC geometries (particularly for viz), but are necessary to robustly determine particle termination in DAGMC simulations. The graveyard volume can be automatically generated at runtime in a DAGMC simulation if a graveyard volume is not already present.

A rectangular shell prism can then be generated that is just larger than the size of the model.

A start for something like this can be found [here](https://github.com/pshriwise/openmc/blob/9ef18f79ed3176a1dd9d487f6ca240fe430c2d68/src/cad.cpp#L9).

title: DAG-MCNP assumes neutron as primary particle all the time- sets cell importances incorrectly
body:
**Describe the Bug**
If you run a DAG-MCNP 6.2 problem with weight windows using a primary mode particle that is not a neutron (eg setting `MODE p` for purely photons) the cell importances get set incorrectly. DAGMC, regardless of particle type, still sets the lcad file with neutron importances in the cells (`imp:n=1` or `imp:n=1`). This causes issues with MCNP then because it will then do the following sequence to set the importances of all the cells: 1. reads the `imp:n` designator from the lcad file and sets cell importances for the neutrons correctly (all volumes get importance 1 except the graveyard that gets importance 0). 2. Sees that we are in mode p for weight windows and tries to read the photon cell importances based on weight window information. Because no information is provided, it defaults all cell importances to 1 (including the graveyard). 3. Then goes back to the neutron importances to update them to match the photon importances because that is the weight window mode particle. After doing this all cells/volumes in the geometry are assigned importance of 1 for both photons and neutrons, including the graveyard volume. These incorrect importances cause lost particles because they are not properly terminated when entering the graveyard. [This](https://github.com/svalinn/DAGMC/blob/develop/src/mcnp/mcnp_funcs.cpp#L272) is where DAGMC default sets the importances of cells as neutron importances with no regard of mode specified in the MCNP input. **To Reproduce**
Run a DAG-MCNP problem in pure photon mode (or just a non neutron mode) that includes weight windows. **Expected Behavior**
What should happen is the cell importances written to the lcad file are `imp:p` if we are in a pure photon mode. Or rather they should match the particle mode specified by the MCNP input. This will cause MCNP to correctly read those importances in as the photon importances in step 1 listed above and not go to steps 2 or 3 to incorrectly overwrite the cell importances. **Additional Context**
Discussed this with @gonuke and there are a few solutions to be considered: - An immediate fix is to alter the lcad file, changing `imp:n` to `imp:p` in the cell lines and rerunning with the changed lcad. This is does work, but is not ideal for a long term solution. - Read the MODE particle specified in the input file. This will be difficult because at the time that DAGMC has to read the geometry and create the lcad file, MCNP has not yet read in MODE card and so we don't yet have that information. - Tag the geometry with a MODE metadata and read it in. If it's not supplied, assume mode n. - Have as an MCNP input option for the user to specify the mode in the MCNP input file on the DAGMC card (would need to do both the MCNP MODE card and this option). Default again can be mode n.

title: Shared library testing on CI and Geant4
body:
So I noticed recently that:

  1. We don't do testing on executables linked to our shared libraries in CI 
  2. When shared testing is enabled, the dagsolid_unit_tests test fails to find some of the libraries it needs and fails on Ubuntu 18.04 only

After some digging, I found that this is because in our 16.04 builds the `RPATH` property of shared libraries and executables is set whereas in 18.04 the `RUNPATH` property is set. This difference is expected as the linking program in Ubuntu, `ld`, moved to using `RUNPATH` in 18.04. (Some links on the difference between these properties and their effects on how libraries are dynamically loaded are at the bottom of this long-winded issue.)

The important difference here is that the `RUNPATH` property won't dynamically load transitive libraries while `RPATH` will. None of the Geant4 libraries have their own `RPATH`/`RUNPATH` properties set -- at least for the installation we rely on in CI anyway. As a result, the libraries, executables, and tests related to Geant4 fail find their dependencies at runtime. Specifically, the problem we run into first is that we link to the `libG5geometry.so` library which in turn links to the `libG4graphics_reps.so` library. These two are in the same location, but because of the `RUNPATH` limitation `libG4graphics_rps.so` isn't found.

I see a couple of options to solve this problem:

__Option 1:__

The Geant4 team seems to be aware that a user's environment needs to be modified to work correctly with their installation and provide a `geant4.sh` in the installation `bin` directory to fix that issue. If we want to count on Geant4 user experience, we can expect that they'll know to source this file before using any of the executables/libraries we produce and things should work just fine. Then we can source this file as part of our test environment or add the Geant4 `lib` directory to the `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for the test and call it good.

__Option 2:__

Ensure that `RPATH` is set instead of `RUNPATH`. This can be done by adding `--disable-new-dtags` to the CMake shared linker flags in the `/src/geant4/` directory which should affect only the targets build in that space.

I'm leaning toward option 1 and have solution in place, but I'd thought I'd explain the problem here and see what others think.

Info on `RPATH` vs. `RUNPATH`:

  - https://gitlab.kitware.com/cmake/community/-/wikis/doc/cmake/RPATH-handling
  - https://medium.com/nataraj-raghavendra/rpath-vs-runpath-883029b17c45

title: Replace LAPACK with Eigen3 for KDE tallies
body:
## Description
This change removes the LAPACK dependency that was embedded in KDE Tallies.  This dependency was only used for solving Ax=b for 3x3 and 4x4 systems.  It has been replaced by Eigen3.

## Motivation and Context
Because LAPACK is a compiled library dependency, there may be conflicts between the compiler used to build LAPACK and the compiler being used to build DAGMC.  This is especially true on shared HPC systems where only certain combinations are available.  Since Eigen3 is a C++ header only library, this potential for conflict is eliminated.

Also, since LAPACK requires FORTRAN, building against LAPACK may impose additional requirements on the environment.

## Changes
This change is an infrastructure change - no bug is fixed and no feature is added.  A small change was made to documentation to mention Eigen3 as a dependency. (Note: Lapack was never explicitly listed as a dependency in the past.)

## Behavior
The behavior has not changed.

title: Model transformations.
body:
In our last community meeting we discussed the value of being able to transform DAGMC models. This is of particular interest in the context of using DAGMC models in combination with CSG geometry as fill universes for CSG cells. In this scenario, it's possible that CAD components may be extracted from a global model, and won't align well with their containing CSG cell. 

As a result of this discussion, the addition of transformation options to the DAGMC API have been proposed. A couple of options I can see to achieve this are:

  1. Store the transformation on the DAGMC instance. All queries to the DAGMC model will undergo an inverse transformation before ray tracing operations on the performed and resulting values will be transformed as needed before being returned.

  2. Transform the mesh model itself. The mesh itself will be transformed upon loading the model before any acceleration data structures are constructed. Queries can then be performed as normal on the transformed model.

Option 1 is more flexible but more costly during runtime. Transformations can be easily applied at any point, and values can be changed relatively easily using wrapper functions around the appropriate queries. Should the need ever arise, multiple transformations (perhaps representing different timesteps) can also be applied. It is also more computationally expensive, however, as each query now requires more floating-point ops.

Option 2 is more rigid but simple and incurs less computational cost during particle transport. Transformations can be applied to each vertex in the mesh to achieve the desired result without any change to how queries are handled at runtime. Multiple transformations or changing transformations would be impractical to support with this approach as they would require updates to the mesh and reconstruction of our acceleration data structures each time the transformation changes. There is also a somewhat unknown factor regarding the effect of changing the orientation of the mesh on the performance of the BVH data structures we rely on for accelerating queries. In the world of a single transformation, this option does allow us to avoid the additional computational overhead of transforming each query. We would instead pay that cost up-front when modifying the coordinates of the mesh vertices.

title: Adding methods for graveyard removal and creation
body:
## Description
This PR adds the following public methods related to graveyard management:

  - `DagMC::remove_graveyard`
  - `DagMC::create_graveyard`
  - `DagMC::has_graveyard`
  - `DagMC::get_graveyard_group`
  - `DagMC::category_tag`

We may want to have a discussion about moving some of these capabilities into the `GeomTopoTool` class in MOAB. If that's the case, that's fine by me but I figured this PR contains the framework and a place to have that discussion :smiley:

## Motivation and Context
These capabilities were added so that models can be exported from Cubit/Trelis with or without a graveyard. The new API functions allow external codes to automatically generate a graveyard volume if one is not present on the model. It also allows an external application to remove the graveyard if needed.

In addition to reducing workflow overhead, the ability to work with models that don't contain a graveyard makes visualization much more convenient.

## Other Information
This PR has a few byproducts that come with it:

  - the `dagmcMetaData::to_lower` method now relies on a common call to the `lowercase_str` method which is provided in the newly added `util.hpp` file. The `lowercase_str` method has been added as part of the `moab` namespace to avoid populating the common namespace (though we may want to have a discussion about our overall namespace situation sometime in the future).
  - the addition of a BBOX struct to the `DagMC` class. This is purely used as a convenience for calculating the global bounding box of the problem when creating a graveyard.
 - the addition of a `DagMC::category_tag` method. This adds some MOAB-specific syntax to DAGMC, but I wasn't sure how else to handle it and it's needed to find the graveyard volume.
  - this adds a test file of a pincell, `pincell.h5m`, that was created in Trelis to ensure that the `remove_graveyard` method works without leaving orphaned entities or entity sets behind.

Resolves #649

title: Unintuitive behaviour for uwuw_preproc with flag -o
body:
Currently, the help message flag for uwuw_preproc describes the behaviour for the flag -o as:
  -o [--output] <arg>: Specify the output filename (default )
I would normally expect an output file  specified by command line to be a new file created by the running the executable. While a new file will be created if one is not already present, it will not contain the mesh geometry, only the metadata. The actual intended usage of the flag, which was not immediately clear, is that the output file already exists and contains the same geometry as the input file provided, and the program is simply appending the metadata. In this sense, in my mind this is just another input file (it just happens to be modified).

I would suggest that
i) The help message is improved to reflect the intended usage.
ii) If the output file is being created, the mesh data is then added, or alternatively the program exits with a failure and/or appropriate warning message that the file doesn't exist.
iii) If the program detects that a file does already exist and is just being appended, there should be a warning to the user that it their prerogative to ensure that the geometry is the same. (I could easily envisage a scenario where the wrong file was appended).
iv) Optionally split cases (ii) and (iii) into having separate flags; perhaps  -c for create and -a for append, and remove -o entirely due to its ambiguity?
v) Presumably tests  should be added for the append/create cases.

We should revisit this logic to prevent excessive calls to track.

title: Checkout PyNE submodule as part of CMake
body:
## Description
Adds an option (default ON) to checkout the PyNE submodule as part of the CMake configuration step.

## Motivation and Context
The addition of this submodule in DAGMC makes updates of PyNE in DAGMC more elegant, but it also requires an extra manual step in DAGMC installation (`git submodule update --init`). There are many build scripts/CI scripts out there that don't include this step and will break as a result.

## Changes
This PR incorporates the submodule initialization and update into the CMake step, meaning that no external build scripts will need to change due to the use of PyNE as a submodule. 

## Behavior
As mentioned above, a section has been added to `CMakeLists.txt` that will checkout the PyNE submodule automatically. If `git` is found on the system, the option `GIT_SUBMODULE` is added with a default value of `ON`. This option can be turned off for development with new versions of PyNE in DAGMC (another benefit of using the submodule as opposed to the previous approach). If `git` is not available, then this option will not appear in the CMake configuration and we will expect that the PyNE submodule is already present in the DAGMC source.

title: Change name of var for make file parallelization
body:
## Description
Change the name of the variable used in CI to manage `make` parallelization from `jobs` to `ci_jobs`.

## Motivation and Context
The variable `jobs` is used in undocumented/poorly documented ways by the `git submodule` command.  We have used a variable with that name in our CI scripts to pass the number of processors to `make -j` for build parallelization.  Changing the name of this variable should allow `git submodule` to work as expected. (as introduced in #734)

Reference: https://github.com/git/git/blame/3a0b884caba2752da0af626fb2de7d597c844e8b/git-submodule.sh
In the last 3-5 years, `git submodule` started using this env variable to expose parallelism to the user.  E.g. Line 547 was added to this file about 3 years ago. Line 50 was added in the above about 12 months ago, indicating a similar problem identified within the git project.  Presumably, newer versions of `git` would not see this problem, just as older versions of `git` did not.


## Changes
This is best described as a bug fix.

## Behavior
Prior to this change, calls to `git submodule` would fail with an unknown pathspec with the same value as the `jobs` variable.

After this change, calls to `git submodule` should work correctly.

title: Scrub references to Trelis

title: Replace individual news files with CHANGELOG update
body:
Currently, our testing requires authors to provide a new entry in the `News` directory connected to their specific PR.  This is intended to help create a Changelog upon release.  However, the effort of compiling many news files is also a burden.  A better solution is to require a change to a single Changelog file.  This has been  implemented in PyNE.

* add a heading in the `doc/CHANGELOG/rst` file for collecting changes for the "Next Version"
* change CI tests to ensure that this file is being changed with each PR
* update documentation to specify how to accomplish this

Note: one useful practice is to require the PR number to be included in  the comment, and to allow some PR's to simply add a new PR number to an existing change description.

I added a namespace to double-down in https://github.com/pshriwise/double-down/pull/29 to protect from clashes of commonly-used class names (`Vec3f`, etc.) and constants with other packages. These are breaking changes with DAGMC that are resolved in this PR. I figured it would be good to get this relatively small issue taken care of before our next DAGMC release.

title: making use of auto-generate release note generate for next release

**Is your feature request related to an enhancement? Please describe.**
On the theme of reducing the amount of work required for releases I wonder if it might be a good time to make use of the new auto-generate release notes feature on github releases. This has a few time saving features - Automatically adds titles of all PRs to a list of features along with links to the PR - Automatically adds all authors of the release as authors on the release - Adds a nice link to a diff showing the changes from previous release to the new release. If we are not happy with the standard layout generated by the auto-generate release notes then we can add a yaml formatting file https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/releasing-projects-on-github/automatically-generated-release-notes#example-configuration In our case this would also allow us to remove the need for adding details to the change log. There would also be one less thing for new contributors to learn before making a PR. **Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**

title: Improvement on Overlap Check Tool
body:
The overlap check tool currently uses a number of points along triangle edges to detect if a piece of the edge exists in more than one DAGMC volume (IC excluded). The number of points along an edge can be changed as an argument to the program, but there will always be gaps and the number of rays fired by the program increases with the number of points requested.

A more robust way to approach this would be to fire rays along the triangle edge to detect intersections with any volumes that are not the parent volumes of the current surface(s) the edge belongs to. This will check for overlaps along the entire edge and the number of rays fired by the program will now be fixed based on the number of triangle edges. To make sure an intersection isn't ignored due to triangle normals we'll either have to fire two rays (one traveling in each direction of the edge) or specify the orientation of desired intersections to the ray tracing kernel -- hopefully the latter to save time.

Note: checking that the triangle vertices are not in another volume via the point containment check is still important to detect fully embedded volumes.

title: Remove need for downstream codes to have Eigen3 installed
body:
**Describe the Bug**
Currently, any downstream code that links to DAGMC must have Eigen3 installed even if it has no direct dependence on Eigen3. Eigen3 is a source-code-header only library, so should be compiled into DAGMC libraries and not necessary to build dependent projects. This problem exists because the DAGMC header is "polluted" with too many other headers. **To Reproduce**
Try to build a downstream code, e.g. OpenMC (see discussion in #739), without having Eigen3 installed. **Expected Behavior**
Build a downstream code that has no independent/direct dependency on Eigen3 without having Eigen3 installed.

title: Remove superfluous headers from DAGMC headers
body:
## Description
Move headers from DAGMC's headers to the implementation files.  Upstream headers only need to be included in header files if details of the classes that those upstream headers define are accessed within the header.  If only the existence of those classes is necessary, then forward declaration of the classes is sufficient.

## Motivation and Context
Since DAGMC's headers may be included by downstream codes, it is good practice to avoid "polluting" our headers with other headers that may, unkown to us, further include other headers and so on.  This 

Fixes #799 

## Changes
Fix of an annoying but non-pathologial bug

title: False positive for assignment of vacuum
body:
@shimwell recently sent me an input with material assignments like "lower_vaccum_vessel", which DAGMC interpreted as a vaccuum assignment. This is caused by the following lines:

https://github.com/svalinn/DAGMC/blob/50caabf16b12179f92e71d4dcfb5bf6090b30cb6/src/dagmc/dagmcmetadata.cpp#L209-L212

Prior to https://github.com/svalinn/DAGMC/commit/cc505bb4e4c70c343542de7b0d2eaa211e031d53, this would not have been a problem since only the presence of "Vacuum" (as opposed to "vacuum") in the material assignment would have triggered this behavior. This is still what I would call a bug, the corner case was just rarer.

I think we either need to document that "V/vacuum" should not be used in material names or only assign volumes a vacuum condition if the lowercase version of the name matches "mat:vacuum" exactly instead of searching for the presence of "vacuum", which is what happens in the lines linked above.

The word vacuum starts to look very strange after typing it so many times at this time of night.

title: Graveyard updates
body:
## Description
These changes update some behavior of the `DagMC::create/remove_graveyard` function. 

### `create_graveyard`
  - `create_graveyard` can now create a graveyard without acceleration data structures using the vertices of the model to create a bounding box as a basis for the graveyard volume.
  - `create_graveyard` will create an implicit complement if none exists so the graveyard volume can be inserted into the model topology correctly.
  - `create_graveyard` will only (re)construct acceleration data structures for the new graveyard volume and the implicit complement if  these data structures were present when the method was initially called.

### `remove_graveyard`

There's a bug when calling `create_graveyard` with `overwrite == true` when a graveyard is not present. Previously, this would fail when trying to remove a graveyard that isn't present. This adds a check at the beginning of `remove_graveyard` to simply return `MB_SUCCESS` if no graveyard is present.

title: Control GeomQueryTool screen output
body:
In Cardinal, we are re-generating an OpenMC DAGMC model on-the-fly based on contours in temperature and density. Each time we re-init DAGMC, the following is printed to the screen

```
Set overlap thickness = 0
Set numerical precision = 0.001
Initializing the GeomQueryTool...
Using faceting tolerance: 0.0001
Building acceleration data structures...
Implicit Complement assumed to be Vacuum
```

In a given simulation, we might be re-initing DAGMC 15 times, so this repeated screen output can de-sensitize the user to our other screen output that we do want them to pay attention to. Ideally, this screen output could be optionally hidden.

title: Add information on representation of metadata and topological relationships
body:
There is some information in the developer's guide on what information exists in our `.h5m` files regarding metadata (meaning material/temperature assignments, boundary conditions, etc.).

It would be useful to developers to describe in more detail what tags are used (`CATEGORY_TAG`, `GEOM_DIM`, etc.), how the metadata is organized in the file ("Group" `EntitySet`'s are tagged with X and contain Y).

Similarly, it would be useful for the developer's guide to contain information on how topological relationships are represented (parent-child relationships) and what each entity set requires to be recognized as a geometric entity (category tag and geom dim tag).

In addition to moving the scripts into a single dockerfile this PR also changes the CI for publishing dockerfiles.
Currently we had a branching and caching approach to the CI dockerfile building that is efficient but complex.

simpler is nice for maintainers :smile:

single dockerfile instead of scripts and simpler CI

title: dagmc tet mesh tallies 5.5x higher when run with MPI version of dag-mcnp6.2
body:
**Describe the Bug**
DAGMC based tet mesh tallies produce values about 5.5x higher with the MPI version of dag-mcnp6.2 as compared to the serial version. The factor of ~5.5 happens independently of how many nodes/cores are used. **To Reproduce**
Run a dag-mcnp6.2 calculation that includes the dagmc tet mesh tallies using the MPI version of dag-mcnp6.2 and run the same calculation with the serial version of dag-mcnp6.2 Then, compare the dagmc tet mesh tally output (recall you will need to convert from h5m to vtk format with mbconvert to easily display or read the output). A simple example with input files and the diff of the vtk dagmc tet mesh tally output file is provided at the UW Box file sharing site: https://uwmadison.box.com/s/zcui19tsc0wepq80icsrva8ampwwvwjr Note the left panel of the diff output is the MPI case and the right panel is the serial case. **Expected Behavior**
We expect that the dagmc tet mesh tally values are the same regardless of whether we run in serial or MPI parallel. **Screenshots or Code Snippets**
None, I have not looked at the source code yet. **Please complete the following information regarding your system:**
- OS: kubuntu linux 18.04-LTS - MOAB Version: 5.1.0 - Physics codes versions installed with: MCNP 6.2 **Additional Context**
All other tallies (including mcnp fmesh structured mesh) produce the same value regardless of whether run in serial or MPI.
